name: ng_apply_item
prose: Precondition: node and item are non-NULL (asserted), the item's hook (if any) carries a reference taken for this call, and the caller has entered the node's read side when rw is NGQRW_R or its write side otherwise. Postcondition: the item's stored hook is taken out of the item. For a data item, an invalid hook or node frees the item and gives EIO; with neither a hook nor a node-type receive-data method the item is freed and 0 is returned; otherwise the receive-data method is called and its result returned (it owns the item). For a message item, an invalid hook is dropped (reference released and hook set to NULL); an invalid node frees the item and gives EINVAL; a generic-cookie message that is not a response goes to ng_generic_msg; with no receive-message method the item is freed and 0 returned; otherwise the method's result is returned. For function items (FN, FN2) an invalid node gives EINVAL and frees the item unless the function is ng_rmnode, and an invalid hook gives EINVAL and frees the item unless the function is ng_con_part2, ng_con_part3 or ng_rmhook_part2; a plain function item is run and freed (error stays 0), an FN2 item is run and its result returned. In all cases the hook reference (if any still held) is released, the read or write side of the node is left, and if the item carried an apply structure: when its depth was 1 and the error is nonzero apply->error is set, and when the last reference to apply is dropped its callback is called with apply->error. The function returns the error value.
note: Read ng_base.c:2364-2506 (comment lines skipped). Reviewer round 15 right: invalid-node EINVAL is skipped for ng_rmnode (2458-2459), and the hook check has its own exemptions (2466-2469); round 1 right: EIO/EINVAL are internal returns. Slice 2340-2597 includes ng_generic_msg start (not part of this record).

name: ng_deflate_decompress
prose: Precondition: node's private data holds an initialized inflate context and DEFLATE_BUF_SIZE inbuf/outbuf buffers, m is a mbuf chain given up to this function, and resultp points to writable storage. Postcondition: *resultp is set to NULL first. If the packet is longer than DEFLATE_BUF_SIZE it counts an error, frees m, resets the sequence number to 0 and returns ENOMEM. m_unshare is then applied (on a NULL result an error is counted and ENOMEM returned, and *resultp stays NULL), the packet is copied into inbuf and the protocol field read (one byte if its low bit is set, else two). For the compressed protocol the received sequence number must equal priv->seqnum, otherwise the packet is freed, the sequence number reset and EPIPE returned; otherwise inflate with Z_SYNC_FLUSH is run into outbuf+1 and any result other than Z_OK or Z_STREAM_END frees m, resets the sequence number and returns ENOMEM (Z_MEM_ERROR), EIO (Z_DATA_ERROR) or EINVAL (other); on success the output (with a zero byte placed in front when the first decompressed byte has its low bit set, so that the protocol field is two bytes, and used as is otherwise) is written back into m with m_copyback and m is trimmed with m_adj, or, if m could not hold it, freed with ENOMEM and the sequence number reset. For an uncompressed protocol the first inflate call (a stored-block header) has its return value overwritten and ignored, a second inflate over the packet (without its leading zero protocol byte if present) must return Z_OK or the packet is freed, the sequence number reset and EINVAL returned, and m itself (unmodified) is returned. On success *resultp is set to m, the sequence number is incremented and 0 is returned.
note: Slice cut the head: real function ng_deflate_decompress (ng_deflate.c:524-699), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: in the uncompressed path the first inflate return is ignored (665 then 678), and only the second must be Z_OK; non-OK in the compressed path maps to ENOMEM/EIO/EINVAL (605-612).

name: ng_l2tp_seq_rack_timeout
prose: Precondition: arg is the node pointer, the caller holds the sequence lock (SEQ_LOCK_ASSERT), seq->xwin[0] is non-NULL and the rack timer is active and not pending (all asserted). Postcondition: returns nothing. It enters the network epoch and the node's vnet, increments xmitRetransmits, and increments seq->rexmits, calling ng_l2tp_seq_failure when the value before the increment was already >= conf.rexmit_max (execution continues afterwards). It re-arms the rack timer with a delay of hz times min(2^rexmits, 2^12 when rexmits > 12, conf.rexmit_max_to), then sets ns to rack, ssth to (cwnd + 1) / 2, cwnd to 1 and acks to 0. It then copies the head packet xwin[0] (L2TP_COPY_MBUF): if the copy fails it releases the sequence lock and increments memoryFailures and nothing is retransmitted; otherwise it calls ng_l2tp_xmit_ctrl(priv, m, seq->ns++), where the post-increment is done by this function as the argument is evaluated, and ng_l2tp_xmit_ctrl itself releases the sequence lock. The vnet and epoch are then left.
note: Read ng_l2tp.c:1431-1480 and the head of ng_l2tp_xmit_ctrl (1487-1504: it stops the xack timer, reads nr, and unlocks SEQ at 1504). Reviewers right: copy failure skips retransmit (1469-1471); ns is incremented by the caller (1473), not in xmit_ctrl. Did not read ng_l2tp_seq_failure (callee).

name: nglmi_newhook
prose: Precondition: node has a softc and name is a NUL-terminated hook name. Postcondition: for the hook named NG_LMI_HOOK_DEBUG it sets the hook's private pointer to NULL and returns 0 even if the node is already connected, setting no protocol state. Otherwise, when the softc already has SCF_CONNECTED it returns EINVAL with nothing changed. For the hooks annexA, annexD and groupof4 it records the hook (lmi_annexA, lmi_annexD or lmi_group4), sets the hook's private pointer to the softc, sets protoID (8, 8, 9), the LMI type and protoname, and calls nglmi_startup_fixed, which marks the softc fixed and connected, stores the channel hook and starts the ticker; for auto0 and auto1023 it records the channel hook, sets protoname to NAME_NONE (and not protoID or the LMI type), sets the hook's private pointer, and calls nglmi_startup_auto (marking auto and connected, resetting the poll state) only when the other auto hook is already present. An unknown name returns EINVAL. All accepted names return 0.
note: Slice cut the head; real function nglmi_newhook (ng_lmi.c:203-253), read in full. Reviewers right: debug hook returns 0 even when connected and sets no protocol state (207-210); auto hooks set only protoname (238-249), protoID/type only on fixed hooks (218-219, 225-226, 232-233).

name: ng_mppc_decompress
prose: Precondition: *datap is an mbuf chain owned by the caller, node private data holds the receive-direction state (history, key, rc4 state, coherency count). Postcondition: m_unshare is applied first and when it returns NULL the function returns ENOMEM leaving *datap unchanged (the chain's fate was not verified here). A packet shorter than the 2-byte MPPC header is freed and EINVAL returned. The header (flags and 12-bit coherency count) is read and stripped, numLost is computed; with the FLUSHED flag the decompression history is reset, and for MPPE the lost count (or lost count divided by the update period) is compared with mppe_max_rekey: above it the packet is freed, EINVAL returned (and the node's receive side disabled when mppe_block_on_max_rekey is set); otherwise keys are updated up to the received count, d->cc is set to the received count and numLost cleared. A nonzero remaining numLost, an encrypted packet when MPPE is not configured, an unencrypted packet when MPPE is configured, or a compressed packet when MPPC is not configured frees the packet and returns EINVAL. An encrypted packet is rc4-decrypted in place (updating the key first in stateless mode or at an update boundary), d->cc is incremented, and a compressed packet is decompressed with MPPC_Decompress into a temporary buffer (ENOMEM with the packet freed if a temporary buffer cannot be allocated, EINVAL with it freed if decompression fails or fills the buffer) and written back into the chain, which becomes NULL if it could not hold the result. On every path that reaches the end *datap is set to the resulting chain and the function returns ENOBUFS if that chain is NULL and 0 otherwise. In the error returns above *datap is not updated.
note: Slice cut the head; real function ng_mppc_decompress (ng_mppc.c:625-835), read in full. Reviewer round 15 is wrong: when the rebuilt chain is NULL (823-825) the function reaches 833-834 and returns ENOBUFS with *datap = NULL; ENOMEM comes only from the allocation/m_unshare paths (636, 776, 789). Reviewer round 1 (m_unshare failure returns ENOMEM without freeing) is consistent with 634-636; I did not verify m_unshare internals.

name: ng_nat_rcvmsg
prose: Precondition: item carries a control message for a ng_nat node whose private data is priv. Postcondition: the message is freed at the end, NG_RESPOND_MSG(error, node, item, resp) is called and the variable error is returned (what the macro does with resp was not read). For typecookie NGM_NAT_COOKIE the cmd is handled: SET_IPADDR (arglen at least sizeof(struct in_addr) else EINVAL) sets the libalias address and the ADDR_DEFINED flag; SET_MODE (arglen check, EINVAL) calls LibAliasSetMode and gives ENOMEM if it returns negative; SET_TARGET sets the target address; REDIRECT_PORT, REDIRECT_ADDR and REDIRECT_PROTO check arglen (EINVAL), allocate an entry (ENOMEM), create the libalias link (ENOMEM and the entry is freed if it is NULL), copy the parameters and description (NUL-terminated), assign the next id, count and append it to the redirect list, and then allocate a response holding the id, giving ENOMEM if that allocation fails after the entry was already added; REDIRECT_DYNAMIC and REDIRECT_DELETE look up an entry by id (ENOENT if absent) and either call LibAliasRedirectDynamic (ENOTTY if it returns -1, entry kept) or LibAliasRedirectDelete, and on success the entry is removed from the list and freed; ADD_SERVER finds the entry by id (ENOENT) and calls LibAliasAddServer (ENOMEM if it returns -1, otherwise lsnat is incremented); LIST_REDIRECTS and LIBALIAS_INFO build a response (ENOMEM if it cannot be allocated); PROXY_RULE needs arglen at least 6 (EINVAL) and gives ENOMEM when LibAliasProxyRule returns nonzero; SET_DLT requires arglen exactly 1 byte equal to DLT_EN10MB or DLT_RAW (EINVAL otherwise). Unknown commands and unknown cookies give EINVAL. A response is attached only for the three redirect-creation commands, LIST_REDIRECTS, LIBALIAS_INFO and the GET_DLT case; otherwise resp is NULL.
note: Slice cut the head; real function ng_nat_rcvmsg (ng_nat.c:363-756), read in full. Reviewer round 15 (NG_RESPOND_MSG sends an error response even with resp NULL) not checked: the macro was not read, so the prose does not claim anything about replies without a body. Note the GET_DLT case is a label of the outer typecookie switch (740), not a command; only its response allocation part (741-745) was visible (line 746 stripped as it was a comment/blank).

name: ng_parse_skip_value
prose: Precondition: s is a NUL-terminated string, off0 is an offset in it, and lenp points to a writable int. Postcondition: it scans tokens from off0 with ng_parse_get_token (which also skips leading white space), counting nested brackets and braces, and stops after the first token if that token is not an opening bracket or brace, or after the token that brings both counts back to zero. On this normal exit it stores in *lenp the distance from off0 to the end of the last scanned token (white space included) and returns 0. It returns EINVAL, without writing *lenp, if the first or any later token is the end of the string (T_EOF), including when an opened bracket or brace is not closed, or if a closing bracket or brace is met while the matching open count is zero (the counts are not cross-checked between brackets and braces except that each type is counted separately). A token that the tokenizer reports as an error (for example an unterminated string, T_ERROR) is not treated specially: its length is whatever the token routine left in the local length (possibly 0), the scan goes on from there, and the function can return 0 with *lenp covering only the preceding white space.
note: Read ng_parse.c:1643-1674 and ng_parse_get_token (1682-1721). Prior prose said *lenp = 0 on EINVAL: wrong; *lenp is written only at 1672 on the normal exit. Reviewer round 1 (unterminated string gives T_ERROR, returns 0 with *lenp not spanning a value) right; round 2 (T_EOF returns EINVAL even with no brackets open) right (1665-1666). Did not read ng_get_string_token in detail (callee).

name: ng_pptpgre_rcvdata_lower
prose: Precondition: hook is the node's lower (IP/GRE) hook and item carries an mbuf starting with an IP header; no session lock is held on entry. Postcondition: increments receive counters, then returns EINVAL (item freed at the done label) for a packet shorter than the IP and GRE headers or than the headers implied by hasSeq/hasAck (recvRunts), for a negative computed extra length or wrong GRE init bits (recvBadGRE), for an unknown, hookless or disabled session (recvBadCID, found by call id), for a late or duplicate sequence number (with the lock released), and for a duplicate already in the reorder queue. A failed m_pullup (counted in memoryFailures) sets the item's mbuf to NULL and returns ENOBUFS (item freed). With the session lock held, an ack (if present) is validated (an ack beyond what was sent, or not newer than recvAck, is ignored), updates recvAck and, when windowing is enabled, the round-trip estimates, send window and ack timers. A packet without a sequence number is counted as a lone ack, the lock released and 0 returned (item freed). For a data packet, the headers and any padding are trimmed; a packet with sequence recvSeq + 1 goes directly to a stack send queue and recvSeq advances; otherwise it is placed in the sequence-ordered reorder queue if the queue length is below reorder_max (stats recvOutOfOrder), and when the queue is full either the current packet goes to the send queue (if it would sit at the head) or the queue head is moved to the send queue and the current packet is queued (recvReorderOverflow). If the queue entry cannot be allocated the queued packets up to the current sequence are flushed to the send queue, ack and the send queue are processed, the current packet is forwarded on the session hook and ENOMEM is returned. In the normal case contiguous entries from the reorder queue are appended to the send queue, the reorder timer is stopped or started depending on whether the queue is empty, and if the send queue is non-empty the lock is dropped by ng_pptpgre_ack and ng_pptpgre_sendq delivers the packets; the function then returns 0. If the send queue is empty it releases the lock and returns 0 with the item held in the reorder queue.
note: Slice cut the head: real function ng_pptpgre_rcvdata_lower (ng_pptpgre.c:749-1058), read in full; the name ng_pptpgre_rcvdata in the packet is a different function (line 509, the send side). Reviewers right: round 15 (it processes received GRE, EINVAL when disabled, no xmit/ENXIO); round 17 (full-queue path may send the current packet instead of moving the head: INIT_SENDQ at 957-958). Not read: ng_pptpgre_ack, ng_pptpgre_sendq (callee internals).

name: ipsec_chkreplay
prose: Precondition: sav and sav->replay are non-NULL (asserted), seqhigh points to a writable uint32_t, seq is the received 32-bit sequence number. Postcondition: returns 1 (accept) or 0 (reject). With replay->wsize == 0 it returns 1 before taking the replay lock and without touching *seqhigh. Otherwise, with the replay lock held, it returns 0 when seq is 0 and replay->last is 0. Otherwise window top tl and th are taken from replay->last and the bottom bl = tl - window + 1: when seq lies in the current window subspace it sets *seqhigh to th and returns 0 if seq <= tl and check_window finds it already seen, else 1. In the other cases: if tl is 0xffffffff and ESN is not enabled, replay->overflow is incremented and, unless SADB_X_EXT_CYCSEQ is set, the wrap statistic is incremented and 0 returned (with CYCSEQ a warning is logged and processing continues); if tl < window - 1 and seq >= bl (previous subspace) it returns 0 when th is 0, else sets *seqhigh to th - 1 and returns 0 if check_window reports a duplicate, otherwise 1; in the remaining (next subspace) case *seqhigh is set to th + 1 (which may be 0 when th is 0xffffffff, in which case overflow is incremented and, unless CYCSEQ is set, it returns 0 after counting the wrap statistic, while with CYCSEQ a warning is logged) and 1 is returned. The replay lock is released before every return after it was taken. The function does not update the replay window.
note: Slice cut the head: real function ipsec_chkreplay (ipsec.c:1273-1398), read in full. Reviewer round 15 right: *seqhigh = th + 1 at 1374 is not necessarily 0; the first overflow check (1331-1347) returns 0 only when CYCSEQ is not set. check_window not read (callee).

name: key_flush_sad
prose: Precondition: the SAD is initialized and now is the current time; the caller holds no SAHTREE lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under the SAHTREE read lock it collects candidates with an extra reference: SAHs with no larval and no alive SAs (empty), larval SAs older than V_key_larval_lifetime (drain), alive SAs whose hard lifetime (addtime, usetime or bytes) has expired (hard-expired), and alive SAs in state MATURE whose soft lifetime has expired or, without ESN, whose replay count or last exceeds 80 percent of the 32-bit space (soft-expired). If nothing was collected it returns. Otherwise under the write lock: drain candidates no longer LARVAL are moved to a free list, the others are unlinked from the larval list and SPI hash and marked DEAD; hard-expired ones already DEAD go to the free list, the others are unlinked from the alive list and SPI hash and marked DEAD; soft-expired ones already DEAD go to the free list, the others are only marked DYING; empty-SAH candidates that now are DEAD or no longer empty simply have their extra reference released with key_freesah (not moved to the free list), and the others are unlinked from the tree and hash and marked DEAD. After unlocking, hard-expired SAs get key_expire(sav, 1) and have the SAH reference and two SA references released, soft-expired SAs get key_expire(sav, 0) and their extra reference released, drained SAs have the SAH reference and two SA references released, free-list SAs have their extra reference released, and empty SAHs have two references released.
note: Read key.c:4710-4913. Reviewers right: soft expiry needs state MATURE at scan time (4774; I also found the replay 80 percent condition at 4781-4784), and changed empty-SAH candidates have their reference dropped immediately (4857-4861), not moved to a free list. Slice 4611-4871 cuts the head and tail of the function.

name: key_updateaddresses
prose: Precondition: so, m, mhp, sav and saidx come from a parsed SADB_UPDATE message; sav is a referenced SA that has not been cloned (SADB_X_EXT_F_CLONED clear, asserted) and is MATURE or DYING (asserted), and saidx is the caller's copy of the SA index. Postcondition: new source and destination addresses found in the message overwrite saidx (ports set to 0). If either new address is present the function returns the error of key_checksockaddrs if it fails, finds the SAH for the new saidx or creates one (ENOBUFS if creation fails); if neither is present it returns EINVAL unless the SA's protocol is ESP and the NAT-T type, sport and dport headers are all present, and then reuses sav's SAH. It allocates a new SA (ENOBUFS), copies sav up to its chain field into it, sets natt NULL, sah to the chosen SAH and state MATURE, and runs key_setnatt on it. Under the SAHTREE write lock it returns ESRCH if sav is already DEAD, otherwise unlinks sav from its SAH and the SPI hash and marks it DEAD, inserts the new SA into the SAH's alive tree ordered by creation time and into the SPI hash, links a newly created SAH into the tree and hash, copies the counters and marks sav CLONED. After unlocking it releases the caller's last reference to sav, builds a reply from m (key_getmsgbuf_x1; ENOBUFS if that fails, after sav has already been replaced, with m not freed) and otherwise frees m, sends the reply up to all sockets and returns 0. The errors returned before the new SA is allocated (checksockaddrs, SAH creation, missing headers) release nothing because nothing was taken yet; the errors after the allocation (allocation failure, key_setnatt error, ESRCH) go to the fail label, which releases the SAH reference (when one was taken or created) and frees the new SA and its natt, leaving the old SA unchanged.
note: Slice cut the head: real function key_updateaddresses (key.c:5355-5552), read in full (the packet name key_update_clone does not exist). The ESRCH path (5469-5473) releases only the new SA and SAH via the fail label. Not read: key_getsah, key_newsah, key_getmsgbuf_x1 (callees).

name: key_setnatt
prose: Precondition: sav->natt is NULL (asserted), sav->sah->saidx is initialized, mhp holds the parsed PF_KEY extension headers. Postcondition: returns 0 without changing anything when the SA protocol is not ESP, or when any one of the SADB_X_EXT_NAT_T_TYPE, SPORT or DPORT headers is absent. When all three are present it returns EINVAL if any of their lengths is wrong, or if the NAT-T type is not UDP_ENCAP_ESPINUDP; it then allocates sav->natt (ENOBUFS and the no-memory statistic on failure) and stores sport and dport, returning EINVAL if either is 0 (the allocation stays attached to sav in that case). The optional OA-initiator and OA-responder headers, when present, must have the right header size (else EINVAL); in non-tunnel mode each is checked for a supported family and length (EINVAL otherwise), stored in natt->oai or natt->oar with the IPSEC_NATT_F_OAI or _OAR flag set only when its address differs from the SA index source or destination respectively (an equal address is ignored), and the one's-complement checksum adjustment of the differing addresses is accumulated and stored in natt->cksum; in tunnel mode the OAI and OAR headers are only length-checked and natt->cksum is left 0. It returns 0 after the checks pass.
note: Read key.c:5966-6176 in full. Reviewers right: equal OAI/OAR addresses are ignored, not copied (6072-6075, 6129-6132); EINVAL for wrong TYPE/SPORT/DPORT lengths only when all three are present (5983-5994, else returns 0 at 5995). Slice cut the head.

name: key_acqreset
prose: Precondition: seq is a 32-bit sequence number; the function takes and releases the ACQ lock itself. Postcondition: it searches the ACQ sequence hash bucket for seq under the ACQ lock; if an entry with acq->seq equal to seq is found, its count is set to 0 and its created time to time_second, and the function returns 0; if none is found no state is changed and it returns ESRCH. No other value is returned and no memory or reference passes to or from the caller.
note: Read key.c:7182-7198. Contract left empty: the function reads and writes the global ACQ hash and lock, so rule 4 does not apply. Slice cut the head; the function is key_acqreset. No reviewer claims beyond the contract mismatch (ESRCH).

name: esp_output
prose: Precondition: m is an mbuf chain for an outbound packet with at least skip bytes before the payload and a protocol byte at protoff, sp and sav are referenced policy and SA objects, sav->tdb_encalgxform is non-NULL (asserted), idx is the transform index; the destination family of the SA is not required to be supported because the function checks it. Postcondition: it computes the ESP header length, padding and authentication length and returns EPFNOSUPPORT when the SA destination family is neither AF_INET nor AF_INET6, or EMSGSIZE when skip + hlen + rlen + padding + alen exceeds IP_MAXPACKET or IPV6_MAXPACKET. It then makes the chain unshared (ENOBUFS on failure), makes room for the ESP header (ENOBUFS), writes the SPI and, when sav->replay exists, increments the replay count and writes the sequence number and saves its high part, copies the counter for CTR/GCM/ChaCha SAs, appends padding and the ICV space with m_pad (ENOBUFS; m_pad frees the chain on failure), fills in padding bytes per the SA's padding mode, the pad length and the original next-protocol byte, and sets the protocol byte to IPPROTO_ESP. It then allocates a crypto request and an xform_data block (ENOBUFS and a crypto statistic on failure), builds the IV, sets up payload, digest and AAD (allocating a separate AAD buffer when the session needs it, ENOBUFS on failure) and dispatches the request, returning the value of crypto_dispatch or crypto_dispatch_async (the chain, sp and sav then belong to the callback esp_output_cb via the xform_data). In each of the error returns listed before the dispatch, the chain (if not already freed) is freed and the references on sav and sp are released with key_freesav and key_freesp.
note: Slice cut the head: real function esp_output (xform_esp.c:699-992), read in full. Reviewer round 15 (precondition requires AF_INET/AF_INET6 yet postcondition returns EPFNOSUPPORT) right: the family is checked at 752-770, so it is not a precondition. Did not read esp_output_cb, crypto dispatch internals.

name: nl_soreceive
prose: Precondition: mp is NULL and uio is non-NULL (asserted), so is a netlink socket with an attached pcb. Postcondition: before taking the receive lock it stores a duplicate of an empty AF_NETLINK source address in *psa when psa is non-NULL, and a NETLINK_MSG_INFO control mbuf in *controlp when controlp is non-NULL and NLF_MSG_INFO is set. It then returns the error of SOCK_IO_RECV_LOCK if the I/O lock cannot be taken, EWOULDBLOCK (after releasing both locks) if the receive queue is empty and the socket is nonblocking (SS_NBIO, MSG_DONTWAIT or MSG_NBIO), or the error of sbwait if waiting for data fails (both locks released); each of these three returns happens without calling nl_on_transmit. Otherwise it scans the queued buffers and counts how many whole netlink messages fit in uio->uio_resid, handling a first oversized message (truncation with MSG_TRUNC, or a partial buffer) and, unless peeking, advances the queue and reduces sb_acc and sb_ccc; with the buffer lock dropped it copies the data with uiomove (once an error occurs it stops copying but still frees the consumed buffers unless peeking), adjusts uio_resid for truncation, adds the message count to the thread's ru_msgrcv, updates *flagsp when flagsp is non-NULL, releases the I/O lock, calls nl_on_transmit and returns the uiomove error (0 if none).
note: Read netlink_domain.c:651-823 in full (lines 672-677 and 815-817 are comment-stripped in my dump; the psa/controlp/flagsp statements were taken from the description of those lines only, partly read). Reviewer round 15 right: the early lock/empty/sbwait error returns (685-686, 698, 704) skip nl_on_transmit (820). Slice cut the head.

name: smb_t2_reply
prose: Precondition: t2p is an initialized TRANS2 request with a request t2p->t2_rq that has been enqueued. Postcondition: the function first calls smb_rq_reply(rqp), which waits for a reply, and returns its error if it fails. If SMBT2_ALLSENT is clear (an interim response to a multi-packet request), it skips to the next record under SMBRQ_SLOCK and returns 0 without placing any data or setting SMBT2_ALLRECV. Otherwise it loops over reply fragments: it reads the word count (ENOENT if below 10), the total parameter and data counts (keeping the smaller values seen), the parameter and data counts, offsets and displacements, returning the error of a failed read, EINVAL when a nonempty parameter or data fragment is not at the expected displacement, then skips the remaining words and byte count and places the data and parameter fragments into t2_rdata and t2_rparam with smb_t2_placedata, returning its error if it fails. When the accumulated parameter and data totals reach the totals, SMBT2_ALLRECV is set and 0 returned; otherwise it moves to the next record under the lock, calls smb_rq_reply again and returns its error if it fails, and repeats.
note: Slice cut the head: real function smb_t2_reply (smb_rq.c:441-543), read in full. Reviewers right: interim response returns 0 without setting SMBT2_ALLRECV (457-460); the function itself calls smb_rq_reply (450, 538), so the reply is not already received. The prior text named EPROTO from smb_t2_placedata: not verified, smb_t2_placedata was not read.

name: smb_t2_request_int
prose: Precondition: t2p points to an initialized TRANS2 request with t2_vc, t2_cred and t2_source valid and with parameter and data chains (possibly empty) in t2_tparam and t2_tdata. Postcondition: it returns EINVAL, before allocating any request and without touching the reply chains, when the parameter or data length exceeds 0xffff, and returns the error of smb_rq_alloc, likewise with no request and nothing torn down, if allocation fails. Otherwise it builds the first TRANSACTION or TRANSACTION2 request carrying as much of the parameters (or parameters and data) as fits in the transmit maximum, enqueues it, sets SMBT2_ALLSENT if everything fit, and calls smb_t2_reply. If data remains it then builds and queues secondary requests in a loop, setting SMBT2_SECONDARY, until everything is sent, then sets SMBT2_ALLSENT and re-initializes the reply chains for reading. Errors from building a fragment, smb_rq_enqueue (skipping smb_iod_removerq as it was not enqueued), smb_t2_reply, smb_rq_new or smb_iod_request are returned. In every path after the request was allocated (success included) the request is released with smb_rq_done (after smb_iod_removerq on paths that got past enqueue), and when an error occurred SMBT2_RESTART is set if the request had SMBR_RESTART and both reply chains are freed with md_done. t2p->t2_rq is left pointing to the request that has been released in those paths.
note: Read smb_rq.c:548-763 in full. Reviewers right: round 1 and 15: early EINVAL and smb_rq_alloc failures return before any request exists and without tearing down reply chains (565, 573, 581-582). I also note the success path falls through bad:/freerq: so smb_iod_removerq and smb_rq_done run on success (736-745), which the prior prose did not state.

name: nbssn_rq_request
prose: Precondition: nbp has a transport socket in nbp_tso, valid nbp_paddr and nbp_laddr names, and a timeout in nbp_timo. Postcondition: it builds and sends a NetBIOS session request (returning the error of mb_init or nb_sosend, with the state unchanged; on send success nbp_state becomes NBST_RQSENT). It then waits for the socket with selsocket: a timeout gives ETIMEDOUT and any other wait error is returned; the reply is read with nbssn_recv and its error returned. For a positive session response it sets nbp_state to NBST_SESSION and NBF_CONNECTED in nbp_flags and returns 0. A reply code that is neither positive nor retarget, or a retarget whose length is not 6, gives ECONNABORTED. For a retarget response it reads the address and port, sets nbp_state to NBST_RETARGET, disconnects, connects to the new address with nb_connect_in and, if that succeeded, recurses into nbssn_rq_request; if either the connect or the recursive call fails it disconnects again and returns that error, and if the recursive call succeeds it returns 0 with the state left by the recursive call (NBST_SESSION after a positive response). The reply chain is freed with md_done when one was received, and the working structures are freed on all returns.
note: Read smb_trantcp.c:191-279 in full. Reviewers right: after a successful retarget recursion the state is NBST_SESSION, not NBST_RETARGET (positive response sets it in the recursive call, 249-251); and the recursive error propagates with a disconnect (268-273). Slice 1-280 cuts the head; this is the function at 191.

name: bootpc_init
prose: Precondition: called once during boot (SYSINIT SI_SUB_ROOT_CONF) in a thread context with the network stack initialized. Postcondition: returns nothing. It returns at once, changing nothing, if nfs_diskless_valid is already nonzero, or if the environment variable vfs.root.mountfrom is set to a value not starting with "nfs:" (a message is printed and the string freed). Otherwise it allocates a global context and, in the normal build, counts broadcast Ethernet-style interfaces; with none it prints a warning and goes to the cleanup label without trying BOOTP. It allocates per-interface contexts, fills them from the interfaces found (panicking if an interface has no link-level hardware address), retrying with pauses until a timeout when none is usable and then calling panic ("no suitable interface") when the timeout expires with no usable interface. It creates a UDP socket (panicking on error), sets up the interfaces, composes and sends the queries with bootpc_call (a failure only prints a message), decodes replies for resolved interfaces, and with the BOOTP_NFSROOT option panics when no root path was offered and there are no root overrides. It adjusts the interfaces, closes the socket, and picks the interface that has a root path, else a resolved one; if none it goes to cleanup. If a root path was received it sets boot.netif.name, adds a default route, mounts the root with md_mount (on failure it panics unless a root override exists, in which case it goes to cleanup), and sets rootdevnames[0] to "nfs:" and nfs_diskless_valid to 3. It then copies the chosen interface's address, broadcast, mask and gateway into the diskless structure. The cleanup label frees the interface contexts and the global context.
note: Slice cut the head: real function bootpc_init (bootp_subr.c:1512-1741), read in full except lines 1520-1538 (declarations) and the BOOTP_WIRED_TO build variant is only partly considered. Reviewers: round 15 (claims panic when no eligible interface but the code warns and returns) is right for the case of zero broadcast interfaces (1596-1599), but the code does panic when interfaces exist and none is usable after the timeout (1644-1656), so the prior wording needed both; round 17 (omits the BOOTP_NFSROOT panic) right (1681-1684).

name: bootpc_received
prose: Precondition: gctx holds a received packet of gctx->replylen bytes in gctx->reply, ifctx is the interface context whose state and dhcpquerytype are initialized. Postcondition: returns 0 without modifying ifctx when the packet has a bad option, when its DHCP message type does not suit the query (for DHCP_DISCOVER: not DHCP_OFFER and, unless BOOTP_FORCE_DHCP is defined, not DHCP_NOMSG; for DHCP_REQUEST: not DHCP_ACK), or when ifctx is already in state IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED, or its query type is DHCP_DISCOVER and its state is IF_DHCP_OFFERED or IF_DHCP_RESOLVED, and either the reply stored in ifctx already has a root-path tag or the new reply has none (IF_DHCP_RESOLVED does not count for a DHCP_REQUEST query). Otherwise it copies the packet into ifctx->reply and updates replylen, then moves the state: IF_BOOTP_UNRESOLVED to IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED; IF_DHCP_UNRESOLVED with a DISCOVER query to IF_DHCP_OFFERED when the reply is an offer and to IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED otherwise; IF_DHCP_OFFERED with a REQUEST query to IF_DHCP_RESOLVED; other states are left as they are (so a repeated message can return 1 with the state unchanged). If the query is DHCP_DISCOVER and the state is not IF_BOOTP_RESOLVED it records the DHCP server id when a 4-byte one is present (setting or clearing gotdhcpserver) and returns 1. Otherwise it sets gotrootpath, gotgw and gotnetmask from the tags of the stored reply and returns 1.
note: Read bootp_subr.c:385-480 in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (returns 1 without advancing state for repeated DISCOVER, e.g. state IF_DHCP_OFFERED, 446-456 has no matching branch); round 15 (IF_DHCP_RESOLVED only counts when dhcpquerytype is DHCP_DISCOVER, 431-433).

name: nlm_setlock
prose: Precondition: host, ext, vers, timo, vp, op, fl, fh, svid, fhlen and size describe a lock request, flags may contain F_WAIT, reclaim says whether this is a reclaim, and retries is the number of RPC retries allowed. Postcondition: it returns the error of nlm_init_lock if building the lock arguments fails. In its retry loop it returns ENOLCK when no RPC client can be obtained (also inside the cancel loop); when the lock RPC does not succeed it deregisters the wait handle (if blocking) and either retries (decrementing retries) or returns EINVAL when retries are used up. For a denied-grace-period reply it sleeps with tsleep (doubling the delay up to 30 seconds) and loops, returning the tsleep error if it is not EWOULDBLOCK. For a blocking request answered nlm4_blocked it waits with nlm_wait_lock: on EWOULDBLOCK it lengthens the delay and loops; on another error it sends cancel requests (repeating with pauses until the RPC succeeds, ENOLCK if no client) and the error from the wait is kept as the result, except that a cancel answered nlm_denied sets the result to 0 on the assumption that the lock was granted. For any other reply the result is nlm_map_status of the status. When the result is 0 and reclaim is false the lock is recorded locally with nlm_record_lock and nlm_host_monitor is called; the function then returns the result.
note: Slice cut the head: real function nlm_setlock (nlm_advlock.c:758-953), read in full. Packet name was unnamed; the final return is at 951, other returns at 782, 792, 812, 832, 874. Did not read nlm_wait_lock or the RPC helpers.

name: cm_sidr_req_handler
prose: Precondition: work is a CM work item whose received MAD is a SIDR REQ, with a valid port and device. Postcondition: it creates a new CM id with ib_create_cm_id and returns that call's error (PTR_ERR) if it fails. Otherwise it fills in the id's address vector from the work completion (cm_init_av_for_lap), the remote id and tid from the request, and increments its work count. Every failure after the id was created takes the out label, which destroys the new id and returns -EINVAL (not the underlying error): a cm_init_av_for_lap failure, a duplicate remote SIDR id (cm_insert_remote_sidr found one; the CM_RECV_DUPLICATES counter for SIDR REQ is incremented), and no listener matching the service id (the request is first answered with cm_reject_sidr_req(IB_SIDR_UNSUPPORTED)). On a match the id's state is IB_CM_SIDR_REQ_RCVD, references are taken on both the new id and the listener, the listener's handler and context are copied into the new id with the service id and mask, the event is formatted, the work is processed by cm_process_work, the listener reference is dropped and 0 is returned.
note: Slice cut the head: real function cm_sidr_req_handler (ib_cm.c: head before 3300, body 3300-3359), read in full. Reviewers both wrong for this source: round 1 (cm_init_av_for_lap failure returns a negative errno) and round 15 (duplicate and no-listener paths leave ret unchanged) -- every goto out ends in return -EINVAL at 3358, and ret is never returned. Not read: cm_insert_remote_sidr, cm_find_listen, cm_process_work.

name: cm_enter_timewait
prose: Precondition: cm_id_priv is a valid cm_id_private with a non-NULL timewait_info. Postcondition: returns nothing. If ib_get_client_data returns NULL for the id's device it returns at once, leaving id.state and cm_id_priv->timewait_info unchanged. Otherwise, under cm.lock, it calls cm_cleanup_timewait on the timewait info (not read here) and appends timewait_info->list to cm.timewait_list, then releases the lock. After the lock is released it sets id.state to IB_CM_TIMEWAIT and converts the address-vector timeout to milliseconds; it takes cm.lock again and, unless the cm_device is going down, queues the timewait work on cm.wq with a delay of that many milliseconds, releases the lock and finally sets cm_id_priv->timewait_info to NULL (also outside any lock).
note: Slice cut the head; real function cm_enter_timewait (ib_cm.c:918-949), read in full. Reviewers right: early return when ib_get_client_data is NULL (925-926), and the state and timewait_info assignments are made outside cm.lock (938, 948). Which trees the cleanup erases from is inside cm_cleanup_timewait (not read).

name: cma_port_from_service_id
prose: Precondition: service_id is a 64-bit big-endian value. Postcondition: returns (u16)be64_to_cpu(service_id), the low 16 bits of the host-order number obtained by converting service_id from big-endian. On a big-endian host this is service_id & 0xffff; on a little-endian host it is the byte-swapped upper 16 bits of the stored value (bswap16(service_id >> 48)). It reads no memory and takes no locks.
note: Read ib_cma.c:1222-1225. Reviewers right (rounds 1, 2, 15): the earlier little-endian formula was wrong; the result is the low 16 bits of the byte-swapped 64-bit value, i.e. bswap16 of the high 16 bits of the stored value on a little-endian host. Contract left empty because it depends on be64_to_cpu and endianness.

name: cma_ib_handler
prose: Precondition: cm_id->context is a valid rdma_id_private whose handler_mutex is initialized. Postcondition: it takes handler_mutex and, if the event is not IB_CM_TIMEWAIT_EXIT and the state is not RDMA_CM_CONNECT, or the event is TIMEWAIT_EXIT and the state is not RDMA_CM_DISCONNECT, it releases the mutex and returns 0 without calling the user handler. It then builds an RDMA CM event from the IB CM event: REQ/REP errors give UNREACHABLE with -ETIMEDOUT; REP_RECEIVED gives CONNECT_ERROR or CONNECT_RESPONSE for SDP according to sdp_verify_rep, and otherwise ESTABLISHED or CONNECT_ERROR from cma_rep_recv when a QP exists, or CONNECT_RESPONSE when none, with the REP data attached; RTU_RECEIVED and USER_ESTABLISHED give ESTABLISHED; DREQ_ERROR (with -ETIMEDOUT), DREQ_RECEIVED and DREP_RECEIVED require cma_comp_exch from CONNECT to DISCONNECT (else it returns 0 without dispatch) and give DISCONNECTED; TIMEWAIT_EXIT gives TIMEWAIT_EXIT; REJ_RECEIVED moves the QP to error and gives REJECTED with the reject data. MRA_RECEIVED and unexpected events (a message is printed for the latter) return 0 without dispatch. The user's event_handler is then called; if it returns nonzero, id_priv->cm_id.ib is set to NULL, the state is exchanged to RDMA_CM_DESTROYING, the mutex is released, the id is destroyed with rdma_destroy_id, and the handler's nonzero value is returned. Otherwise the mutex is released and 0 is returned.
note: Read ib_cma.c:1968-2051 in full. Reviewer round 15 is wrong: the code does clear id_priv->cm_id.ib (2042) and returns the handler result ret (2046). Reviewer round 1 right: MRA, default and failed comp_exch exit without dispatch, not only the incompatible-state case.

name: rdma_resolve_addr
prose: Precondition: id is a valid rdma_cm_id and dst_addr is a valid sockaddr (src_addr may be NULL). Postcondition: if the id is in RDMA_CM_IDLE it first calls cma_bind_addr and returns its error if it fails (the state then is whatever that call left, not changed by this function). It returns -EINVAL when the id's address family differs from dst_addr->sa_family or when the state cannot be moved from RDMA_CM_ADDR_BOUND to RDMA_CM_ADDR_QUERY. After that move it takes an extra reference, copies dst_addr, and resolves it: through cma_resolve_loopback for an any address, cma_resolve_ib_addr for AF_IB, otherwise cma_check_linklocal followed by rdma_resolve_ip with addr_handler as callback. It returns 0 when that step succeeded, with the id in RDMA_CM_ADDR_QUERY and the extra reference to be released by the asynchronous handler; when that step returned an error, the state is set back to ADDR_BOUND (cma_comp_exch from ADDR_QUERY), the reference is dropped and the error of cma_resolve_loopback, cma_resolve_ib_addr, cma_check_linklocal or rdma_resolve_ip is returned.
note: Slice cut the head; real function rdma_resolve_addr (ib_cma.c:3074-3119), read in full. Reviewers right: round 15 (errors of cma_resolve_loopback and cma_resolve_ib_addr are returned, 3097-3100, 3111-3118); round 1 (cma_bind_addr failure returns without any state restore, 3083-3085). The prior statement that the state is always left unchanged on error was wrong: after the move to ADDR_QUERY the state is restored to ADDR_BOUND (3116).

name: cma_remove_id_dev
prose: Precondition: id_priv is a valid rdma_id_private registered with the device being removed. Postcondition: the state is exchanged to RDMA_CM_DEVICE_REMOVAL with cma_exch; if the previous state was RDMA_CM_DESTROYING the function returns 0 at once (handler_mutex was never taken, nothing cancelled and no handler called). Otherwise it calls cma_cancel_operation for the previous state, takes handler_mutex, and if the state is no longer RDMA_CM_DEVICE_REMOVAL it releases the mutex and returns 0 without calling the handler; otherwise it calls id_priv->id.event_handler with an RDMA_CM_EVENT_DEVICE_REMOVAL event, releases the mutex and returns the handler's return value (the caller cma_process_remove destroys the id when this is nonzero).
note: Slice cut the head; real function cma_remove_id_dev (ib_cma.c:4571-4595), read in full, with the caller cma_process_remove (4612-4615). Reviewers right: DESTROYING and failed cma_comp give 0 without the handler; the early return does not hold handler_mutex.

name: iw_cm_listen
prose: Precondition: cm_id is a valid iw_cm_id embedded in an iwcm_id_private; a backlog of 0 is replaced by default_backlog. Postcondition: it first calls alloc_work_entries for the backlog, before looking at the state, and returns its error if it fails (the state is not changed and nothing else is done). It then takes the id lock and, if the state is IW_CM_STATE_IDLE, sets it to IW_CM_STATE_LISTEN, drops the lock, calls iw_cm_map and, when that succeeds, the device's create_listen with the backlog; if either fails the state is set back to IW_CM_STATE_IDLE and the error (negative errno) is returned, otherwise 0 is returned. If the state is not IDLE it returns -EINVAL, after the work entries were already allocated. The lock is released before the return in the paths where it was taken.
note: Slice cut the head; real function iw_cm_listen (ib_iwcm.c:454-488), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (backlog 0 defaults, alloc failure does not revert state because it happens before any state change, 462-467); round 15 (alloc_work_entries runs first, so the -EINVAL case can follow a successful allocation).

name: process_rmpp_ack
prose: Precondition: agent is a valid MAD agent private and mad_recv_wc holds a received RMPP ACK MAD. Postcondition: returns nothing. A nonzero rmpp_status calls abort_send and nack_recv with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_BAD_STATUS and returns; newwin < seg_num does the same with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_W2S. Otherwise, under the agent lock, it looks up the matching send: with none, an ACK with seg_num 0 is passed to process_ds_ack and the function then returns (any other unmatched ACK just returns). If last_ack equals the segment count and the timeout is set (a repeated ACK for a DS transaction) the lock is dropped and ack_ds_ack is called. If last_ack equals the segment count, or no timeout is set, or the send status is not success, the ACK is ignored. If seg_num exceeds the segment count or the current newwin of the send, the lock is dropped and abort_send and nack_recv are called with IB_MGMT_RMPP_STATUS_S2B. An old ACK (newwin smaller than the recorded newwin, or seg_num below last_ack) is ignored. Otherwise, only when seg_num is greater than last_ack, last_ack is advanced and retries_left reset; newwin is then stored. If last_ack now equals the segment count the send is completed (when the buffer has no timeout the MAD is marked done and completed with success) or the timeout is reset and ack_ds_ack called; otherwise, when the send's refcount is 1 and more segments can be sent within the window, the next segment is sent with send_next_seg and, if that succeeds, refcount is incremented and the send moved to the tail of the agent's send list. The agent lock is released before each return after it was taken.
note: Slice cut the head; real function process_rmpp_ack (ib_mad_rmpp.c:659-751), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (S2B abort/nack when seg_num exceeds the segment count or newwin, 701-706); round 15 (last_ack and retries_left updated only when seg_num > last_ack, 712-715).

name: uapi_merge_def
prose: Precondition: uapi and ibdev are valid; def_list is NULL or an array of uapi_definition entries terminated by an entry of kind UAPI_DEF_END. Postcondition: a NULL def_list returns 0 at once. Otherwise the entries are processed in order and the function returns 0 when UAPI_DEF_END is reached. A CHAIN entry recurses on its chained list and returns its error if nonzero; a CHAIN_OBJ_TREE entry gives -EINVAL after a WARN_ON when the entry's object id differs from the tree's id, else it sets the current object key and returns the error of uapi_merge_obj_tree if nonzero; the IS_SUPPORTED_DEV_FN and IS_SUPPORTED_FUNC entries do nothing when the device supports the function and otherwise call uapi_disable_elm, returning its error if nonzero; OBJECT_START sets the current object key and adds the object element with uapi_add_get_elm, returning its error (PTR_ERR) on failure; WRITE calls uapi_create_write with the current keys and returns its error if nonzero; an unknown kind gives -EINVAL after a WARN_ON. The function returns the first nonzero error encountered, leaving earlier merges in place.
note: Slice cut the head; real function uapi_merge_def (ib_uverbs_uapi.c:273-352), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (a NULL list is accepted as empty, 283-284; termination is UAPI_DEF_END, 306-307); round 15 (the error of uapi_merge_obj_tree is returned, 300-303).

name: __ipoib_ib_dev_flush
prose: Precondition: priv is a valid IPoIB device private structure with an initialized vlan_mutex and child_intfs list, level is an ipoib_flush_level value. Postcondition: returns nothing. Under vlan_mutex it first calls itself for every child interface with the same level and then releases the mutex. It then returns without doing anything more if IPOIB_FLAG_INITIALIZED is clear or IPOIB_FLAG_ADMIN_UP is clear. For IPOIB_FLUSH_HEAVY: if ib_find_pkey fails it clears IPOIB_PKEY_ASSIGNED, brings the device down and stops it and returns if ipoib_pkey_dev_delay_open returns true; otherwise (including after a find failure when delay_open is false) it sets IPOIB_PKEY_ASSIGNED with test_and_set_bit and returns without further work if that bit was already set and new_index equals priv->pkey_index (this return cannot happen right after a failed find, because the bit was just cleared), else it stores new_index as pkey_index (after a failed find new_index is whatever ib_find_pkey left it). For IPOIB_FLUSH_LIGHT it marks paths invalid and flushes the multicast state; for levels at or above NORMAL it calls ipoib_ib_dev_down; for HEAVY it also stops and reopens the device. Finally, if ADMIN_UP is still set it calls ipoib_ib_dev_up for levels at or above NORMAL and runs ipoib_mcast_restart_task.
note: Slice cut the head; real function __ipoib_ib_dev_flush (ipoib_ib.c:881-948), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (early return when ipoib_pkey_dev_delay_open is true, 913-914); round 15 (after ib_find_pkey failure PKEY_ASSIGNED is cleared so the unchanged-index early return cannot follow, 910, 918-922).

name: sdp_connect_handler
prose: Precondition: sk is a listening SDP socket, id is the incoming rdma_cm_id and event->param.conn.private_data points to a readable struct sdp_hh (its max_adverts, bsdh.bufs and localrcvsz fields are read without a NULL or length check). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL without creating a child when h->max_adverts is 0, -ENOMEM when sonewconn fails, and the error of sdp_init_qp(child, id) when that fails, in which case the child socket created by sonewconn is not released here and the function does not touch the new ssk. On success it takes the child's write lock, sets id->context to the child's sdp_sock, ssk->id, ssk->socket and a held credential, copies the remote port and address and only the local port (lport) from the id's route (the local address is not set here), sets max_bufs and the tx credits from the hello header, min_bufs as a quarter of the credits, xmit_size_goal from localrcvsz less the BSDH size, initializes the buffers with rcvbuf_initial_size, sets the state to TCPS_SYN_RECEIVED, releases the lock and returns 0.
note: Slice cut the head; real function sdp_connect_handler (sdp_cma.c:142-187), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (child socket not freed on sdp_init_qp failure, 165-167); round 15 (only lport is set from the local address, 177).

name: sdp_cma_handler
prose: Precondition: id and event are the rdma_cm callback arguments; id->context is NULL or an sdp_sock whose socket and id fields may themselves be NULL. Postcondition: if id->context is NULL, or its socket or id is missing, it returns -EINVAL for RDMA_CM_EVENT_CONNECT_REQUEST and 0 for any other event, changing nothing. Otherwise it dispatches on event->event and sets rc: ADDR_RESOLVED (-ENETUNREACH if only IB link layers are allowed and the port's is not, else rdma_resolve_route's result); ADDR_ERROR (-ENETUNREACH); ROUTE_RESOLVED (sdp_init_qp, then builds a hello and rdma_connect); ROUTE_ERROR (-ETIMEDOUT); CONNECT_REQUEST (sdp_connect_handler; on failure rdma_reject; on success builds a hello-ack and calls rdma_accept, and if that fails clears ssk->id, id->qp and id->context of the new child sdp_sock); CONNECT_RESPONSE (sdp_response_handler, with rdma_reject on error, else rdma_accept); CONNECT_ERROR (-ETIMEDOUT); UNREACHABLE (-ENETUNREACH); REJECTED (-ECONNREFUSED); ESTABLISHED (sdp_connected_handler); DISCONNECTED (clears qp_active, rdma_disconnect, and, unless the state is TCPS_TIME_WAIT, rc = -EPIPE if sdp_disconnected_handler returns nonzero); TIMEWAIT_EXIT (sdp_disconnected_handler's result); DEVICE_REMOVAL (-ENETRESET); anything else prints a message and gives -ECONNABORTED. If rc is nonzero afterwards the function takes the socket's write lock and, only when ssk->id still equals id, clears ssk->id, id->qp and id->context and calls sdp_notify(ssk, -rc) (which, when it returns nonzero, leaves the lock released by itself), otherwise releases the lock; it returns rc.
note: Slice cut the head; real function sdp_cma_handler (sdp_cma.c:268-463), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (early torn-down CONNECT_REQUEST returns -EINVAL without clearing anything, 282-288); round 15 (rdma_accept failure clears the child ssk->id/id->qp/id->context at 371-375 before the common block, where ssk (reassigned to the child at 353) has ssk->id != id). Not read: sdp_notify, sdp_init_qp.

name: sdp_wait_rdmardcompl
prose: Precondition: ssk->tx_sa is non-NULL, timeo_p points to the remaining timeout, the caller holds the socket lock (which is dropped while sleeping through posts_handler_put and re-taken with posts_handler_get). Postcondition: the function loops while ssk->qp_active is set. In the loop it breaks with -ETIME and TX_SA_TIMEDOUT set when *timeo_p is 0; with -EINVAL and TX_SA_ERROR set when bytes_acked exceeds bytes_sent; with -EAGAIN when TX_SA_SENDSM is set in the abort flags; and, when ignore_signals is 0, with -EINTR and TX_SA_INTRRUPTED if a signal is pending, or with -ETIME and TX_SA_CROSS_SEND if ssk->rx_sa is set while bytes_acked < bytes_sent. Otherwise it sleeps (sk_wait_event on a local copy of the timeout) and breaks with err 0 when bytes_acked equals bytes_sent after waking. After the loop, if ssk->qp_active is clear it returns -EINVAL (whatever err was, and without setting any abort flag); otherwise it returns err. *timeo_p is not modified by this function.
note: Read sdp_zcopy.c:150-239 in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (QP destroyed gives -EINVAL with no TX_SA abort flag, 234-236); round 15 (*timeo_p is never written, only the local current_timeo is). Slice cut the head.

name: crypto_cursor_advance
prose: Precondition: cc is an initialized crypto buffer cursor and amount does not exceed the bytes left in its buffer (asserted with MPASS only for CRYPTO_BUF_CONTIG and CRYPTO_BUF_SINGLE_MBUF; the other types rely on the caller). Postcondition: returns nothing and advances the cursor by amount bytes according to cc_type. CONTIG: cc_buf advances and cc_buf_len decreases by amount. MBUF: cc_offset grows within the current mbuf when amount is smaller than the bytes left in it; otherwise whole mbufs are consumed (cc_mbuf moved to m_next with cc_offset 0) until the amount is used up; cc_buf_len is not modified. SINGLE_MBUF: cc_offset += amount (cc_mbuf unchanged). VMPAGE: cc_buf_len is decreased by amount for a partial advance within a page, or by the bytes left in each page consumed (cc_vmpage incremented, offset 0), stopping when amount is used up or cc_buf_len reaches 0. UIO: cc_offset grows within the current iovec for a partial advance without changing cc_buf_len; for each whole iovec consumed cc_buf_len is decreased by its remaining bytes, cc_iov is incremented and cc_offset set to 0. For an invalid type it panics under INVARIANTS and does nothing otherwise.
note: Slice cut the head; real function crypto_cursor_advance (criov.c:334-401), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (cc_buf_len not updated for MBUF, nor for a partial UIO advance, 345-357, 383-385); round 15 (VMPAGE partial advance decreases cc_buf_len by amount, 367-370).

name: crypto_done
prose: Precondition: crp is a completed request whose crp_session, crp_callback and crp_retw_id are valid and whose crp_flags and crp_seq were set by the submitter. Postcondition: returns nothing. If crp_etype is nonzero the error statistic is incremented. If CRYPTO_F_ASYNC_ORDERED is clear and either CRYPTO_F_CBIMM is set or CRYPTO_F_CBIFSYNC is set and the session is synchronous, crp->crp_callback(crp) is called directly in this context. Otherwise the request is queued on its return worker under the worker's lock: with CRYPTO_F_ASYNC_ORDERED it is inserted into crp_ordered_ret_q in ascending crp_seq order (after the last entry with a smaller sequence found scanning from the tail, or at the head if none) and the worker is woken if crp_seq equals reorder_cur_seq; without it, it is appended to the tail of crp_ret_q and the worker is woken if that queue was empty. The lock is released after the optional wakeup_one.
note: Slice cut the head; real function crypto_done (crypto.c:1667-1729), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (immediate callback also requires ASYNC_ORDERED clear, 1679); round 15 (ordered insertion is ascending by crp_seq, 1702-1716, not descending).

name: ktls_ocf_tls_cbc_encrypt
prose: Precondition: tls->sync_dispatch is true (asserted), outiovcnt + 1 <= m->m_epg_npgs + 2 (asserted), m is an unmapped TLS record mbuf; with INVARIANTS and an implicit IV the caller must not run another encryption on this session at once (asserted) and m->m_epg_seqno must equal os->next_seqno. Postcondition: under INVARIANTS with an implicit IV a sequence mismatch prints a message and returns EINVAL with nothing else changed; otherwise in_progress is set. It computes the MAC over the pseudo-header and record payload with the MAC session; if that dispatch fails the error is returned with the record not modified yet (the padding has not been written), after clearing in_progress under INVARIANTS. Otherwise it writes the TLS CBC padding bytes into the trailer after the MAC, then dispatches the CBC encryption of the payload and trailer, in place or, when outiov is non-NULL, to the output iovecs, with the IV taken from os->iv (implicit IV) or from the record header (explicit IV). For an implicit IV the function afterwards copies the last AES block of the record's trailer (read from the mbuf's trailer buffer, not from outiov) into os->iv, and under INVARIANTS sets os->next_seqno to m_epg_seqno + 1 and clears in_progress; this happens whether or not the encryption dispatch returned an error. It returns the error of the encryption dispatch (0 on success).
note: Slice cut the head; real function ktls_ocf_tls_cbc_encrypt (ktls_ocf.c:272-417), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (the IV, next_seqno and in_progress updates at 404-415 run even when the encryption dispatch failed, and the trailer padding was already written at 364-366); round 15 (the IV is read from the mbuf trailer, 407, even with a separate outiov).

name: moea_pte_spill
prose: Precondition: addr is a virtual address; the caller does not hold moea_table_mutex. Postcondition: increments moea_pte_spills and takes moea_table_mutex, releasing it before each return. It computes the primary PTEG index from the segment register and addr, picks a pseudo-random slot i (low bits of the time base) in that PTEG, and scans that PTEG's pvo list. For the first pvo whose PTE matches addr it calls moea_pte_insert: if that returns a slot (>= 0) the pvo's PTEG index is set, moea_pte_overflow is decremented and it returns 1 immediately; otherwise that pvo becomes the source. It also looks for a victim pvo whose PTE equals the PTE currently in slot i (only when that PTE is in the primary hash). If no source pvo was found it returns 0 with no change. If a source was found but no victim in the primary list, it panics when slot i's PTE is not a secondary-hash entry and otherwise searches the secondary PTEG's list for the victim, panicking if none exists. With a source and a victim it clears the HID bit in the source's PTE, unsets the victim's PTE in slot i, sets the source's PTE there, clears the victim's PTEG index, sets the source's index to i, increments moea_pte_replacements and returns 1.
note: Slice cut the head; real function moea_pte_spill (mmu_oea.c:2317-2428), read in full. Reviewers: round 1 and round 2 about preconditions/mutex are consistent with 2336-2383; round 15 (the return-1 path omits moea_pte_insert and the overflow count) right, the first-match insert path at 2354-2360 was missing; I did not read moea_pte_insert, so I do not claim how overflow is adjusted inside it.

name: mmu_radix_advise
prose: Precondition: pmap is a valid pmap and [sva, eva) a range of its addresses. Postcondition: for any advice other than MADV_DONTNEED or MADV_FREE it returns at once without taking the pmap lock or changing anything. Otherwise it holds the pmap lock while walking the range by 1GB, 512GB and 2MB steps, skipping invalid upper-level entries. A valid non-managed 2MB leaf mapping is skipped; a valid managed one is demoted with pmap_demote_l3e_locked: if the demotion fails (the mapping was destroyed, nothing removed) the range is skipped; if it succeeds and the old mapping was not wired, the PTE of the last page of the range within that 2MB region is removed with pmap_remove_pte (and anychanged set). Then each PTE of the range that is both managed and valid is processed: if it is modified and writable, then for MADV_DONTNEED its page is first marked dirty, and for either advice the modified and accessed bits are cleared; else if only the accessed bit is set it is cleared; other PTEs are left alone. If anything changed, pmap_invalidate_all(pmap) is called. The lock is released before returning.
note: Slice cut the head; real function mmu_radix_advise (mmu_radix.c:2218-2334), read in full. Reviewers right: round 1 (PG_M is cleared for MADV_FREE writable pages too, 2315, while vm_page_dirty is only for DONTNEED, 2306-2313); round 15 (the demotion failure path, 2260-2267, leaves the range skipped with no page removed).

name: mmu_radix_dev_direct_mapped
prose: Precondition: pa and size describe a physical address range. Postcondition: returns the value of mem_valid(pa, size) (mem_valid was not read here; the previous text assumed it returns 0 or EINVAL). The function takes no locks and has no other side effects apart from a trace macro.
note: Read mmu_radix.c:6159-6164. Contract left empty: depends on mem_valid (callee not read). Reviewers (rounds 1, 2, 15) only complained that the formal contract omitted EINVAL.

name: mmu_radix_change_attr
prose: Precondition: va and size describe a kernel virtual address range, mode is a memory attribute. Postcondition: it takes the kernel_pmap lock, calls pmap_change_attr_locked(va, size, mode, true), releases the lock and returns that function's result, which can be 0, EINVAL, ENOMEM or an error of a recursive direct-map call. The lock is released before the return and nothing is returned to the caller except that status.
note: Read mmu_radix.c:6206-6216. Contract left empty (it takes a lock on a global pmap and the result set comes from pmap_change_attr_locked).

name: pmap_change_attr_locked
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the kernel_pmap lock (asserted), va and size describe a kernel address range, mode is a memory attribute, flush says whether to flush caches. Postcondition: the range is rounded to whole pages. It returns EINVAL if the rounded base is below DMAP_MIN_ADDRESS. A first pass over the range returns EINVAL if an L2, L3 or PTE entry is absent or zero, skips 1GB and 2MB leaf mappings that already have the requested attribute or are fully covered, and demotes other large leaf mappings (ENOMEM if a demotion fails); demotions made before a later failure stay in place. A second pass sets the attribute bits of each leaf, L3 and PTE entry whose attribute differs (recording that something changed) and collects runs of kernel-virtual physical ranges below dmaplimit, applying pmap_change_attr_locked recursively to the corresponding direct-map addresses; an error from a recursive call stops the pass (partial changes remain) and is returned, and a last pending run is also applied if no error occurred. If anything changed it calls pmap_invalidate_all(kernel_pmap) and, when flush is true, flushes the cache range from the base to the last address reached, also when a recursive call failed. It returns 0 only when no error occurred.
note: Read mmu_radix.c:6219-6424 in full. The prior statement that it sets every page and returns 0 was an overclaim: recursive direct-map calls can fail and leave partial changes (6335-6339, 6409-6410, 6423). Contract left empty. No separate reviewer claims beyond the contract omissions.
